questions.question: ______ is the branch of agriculture that deals with feeding, shelter, health, and breeding of domestic animals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Animal Husbandry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Animal husbandry is the branch of agriculture concerned with the care, breeding, and management of domestic animals such as cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, horses, and poultry.
 
• It involves providing proper shelter, feeding, disease prevention, and breeding practices to enhance productivity and ensure the welfare of animals.
 
• Animal husbandry plays a significant role in the rural economy by providing livelihood opportunities and contributing to the production of milk, meat, eggs, and other animal-based products.
 
• The practice helps in improving the genetic traits of animals through selective breeding and modern biotechnology methods.
 
• It is a critical component of sustainable agriculture and food security, ensuring the availability of animal-derived food products globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Aquaculture:** The cultivation of aquatic organisms like fish, shellfish, and seaweed under controlled conditions for food and other purposes.
 
• **Poultry Farming:** A specialized branch of animal husbandry focused on raising domestic birds like chickens, ducks, and turkeys for meat and eggs.
 
• ** A technique used in animal husbandry to breed animals with desirable traits to improve productivity and quality.
 
• Livestock Management:** Includes all practices related to feeding, health care, housing, and breeding to ensure the optimal productivity and welfare of domestic animals.

• In a field, many other **undesirable plants** may grow naturally along with the crop. These undesirable plants are called **weeds**.

• **Weeds **may also act as alternate hosts for many stages of insect pests and pathogens.

• It gives advantages to utilizing crops themselves as tools for weed management.

questions.question: Large scale storage of grains is done in :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silos and granaries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Silos** are tall cylindrical structures used for the large-scale storage of grains, particularly in modern agricultural systems.
 
• **Granaries** are traditional storage structures used for grain storage, often found in rural areas or older systems.
 
• Both silos and granaries protect stored grains from environmental factors such as moisture, pests, and rodents, ensuring long-term preservation.
 
• Grains are stored in these structures after proper drying to prevent spoilage due to fungal growth or microbial activity.
 
• These facilities are essential for maintaining food security and ensuring a stable grain supply throughout the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silos:**

 
 
• Silos are airtight and designed to store large quantities of grains or other agricultural products.
 
• They can be made of concrete, steel, or other durable materials, and often include features like temperature control systems.
 
• They are widely used in industrial-scale agriculture to manage bulk storage and distribution of grains.
 
 
 
• **Granaries:**
 
 
• Granaries are smaller, traditional storage systems, often made of wood, mud, or bamboo.
 
• They are generally located near farms or agricultural fields and are used for community or household grain storage.
 
• They are effective in rural or small-scale farming systems.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Grain Storage:**
 
 
• Improper storage can lead to post-harvest losses due to pests, moisture, and fungal contamination.
 
• Modern storage systems, such as silos, incorporate pest control and ventilation systems to address these challenges.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Proper Grain Storage:**
 
 
• Ensures food security by preventing spoilage and loss of harvested grains.
 
• Supports price stabilization by allowing surplus grain to be stored for future use.
 
• Helps in maintaining the quality of grains for consumption and trade.

questions.question: Which of the following is not likely to increase the fertility of soil?

options.text: Grow different crops alternately every season
Maintain minimum distance between the crops while sowing
Leave the field uncultivated between two crops

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Maintain minimum distance between the crops while sowing**

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• Soil fertility refers to the ability of soil to provide essential nutrients to plants in adequate amounts for their growth and development.
 
• Several agricultural practices can significantly enhance soil fertility, including crop rotation, organic manure use, and allowing fields to rest.

**Explanation:**__

 
• **Grow different crops alternately every season:** This practice, known as crop rotation, helps prevent soil depletion of specific nutrients, reduces pest and disease cycles, and improves soil structure and organic matter content. It contributes significantly to maintaining and enhancing soil fertility.
 
• **Maintain minimum distance between the crops while sowing:** Adequate spacing between crops can enhance plant growth by reducing competition for sunlight, water, and nutrients. However, this practice primarily focuses on optimizing plant growth rather than directly increasing soil fertility.
 
• **Substitute fertilizers by organic manure:** Using organic manure such as compost or green manure enriches the soil with essential nutrients, improves soil structure, increases water retention, and promotes beneficial microbial activity. This practice is highly effective in enhancing soil fertility.
 
• **Leave the field uncultivated between two crops:** Also known as fallowing, this practice allows the soil to recover its nutrient levels naturally, improves its structure, and reduces the buildup of pests and diseases. This rest period can lead to increased fertility and better crop yields in subsequent planting seasons.

questions.question: Dead plants and animals return nitrogen to the soil as which of the following?
questions.solution:
Dead plants and animals return nitrogen to the soil as** Ammonium Compounds.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Nitrogen **is a constituent of **amino acids, proteins, hormones, chlorophylls, and many vitamins.**
 
• Our atmosphere has **78%** nitrogen gas.
 
• **Nitrogen **is one of the essential constituents of all living organisms as part of proteins, chlorophyll, nucleic acids, and vitamins.
 
• Plants compete with microbes for the limited **nitrogen **that is available in the soil.
 
• Thus, **nitrogen **is a limiting nutrient for both natural and agricultural ecosystems.
 
• The **atmospheric nitrogen** cannot be taken directly by plants and animals.
 
• Certain bacteria and blue-green algae present in the soil **fix nitrogen** from the atmosphere and convert it into compounds of nitrogen.
 
• Once **nitrogen **is converted into these usable compounds, it can be utilized by plants from the soil through their root system.
 
• **Nitrogen **is then used for the synthesis of plant proteins and other compounds.
 
• Animals feeding on plants get these proteins and other **nitrogen compounds.**
 
• When plants and animals die, bacteria and fungi present in the soil convert the **nitrogenous wastes into nitrogenous compounds** to be used by plants again.

questions.question: Which of the following is a group of protein rich foods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Egg, Chicken and Almonds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proteins** are essential macronutrients required for the growth, repair, and maintenance of body tissues. They are made up of amino acids, which are considered the building blocks of life.
 
• Foods rich in protein include animal-based sources like **meat, poultry (e.g., chicken), fish, eggs**, and plant-based sources such as **nuts, seeds (e.g., almonds), lentils, and beans**.
 
• **Eggs** are considered a complete protein source as they contain all the essential amino acids that the body cannot produce on its own. They are also rich in vitamins and minerals, making them a nutritious food choice.
 
• **Chicken** is another excellent source of high-quality protein. It is widely consumed and provides essential nutrients like **vitamin B6, phosphorus, and niacin**, which support energy metabolism.
 
• **Almonds**, a plant-based source of protein, are rich in nutrients such as **vitamin E, magnesium, and healthy fats**. They are also a good option for vegetarians and vegans to supplement their protein intake.
 
• Option 1 (Mango, Banana, and Almonds) is not correct because while almonds are protein-rich, mangoes and bananas are primarily rich in **carbohydrates and vitamins**.
 
• Option 2 (Potato, Lemon, and Tomato) is not correct as these are primarily sources of **carbohydrates, fiber, and vitamin C**, not rich in protein.
 
• Option 4 (Egg, Bread, and Almonds) is incorrect because while eggs and almonds are protein-rich, bread is primarily a source of **carbohydrates**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Egg, Chicken, and Almonds.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Proteins:**

 
 
• **Proteins** play a crucial role in building and repairing tissues, producing enzymes and hormones, and supporting immune functions.
 
• They are vital for the growth and maintenance of muscles, skin, and other body structures.
 
• Proteins provide **4 calories per gram**, making them a significant source of energy.
 
 
 
• **Sources of Protein:**
 
 
• Animal-based protein sources include **meat, fish, eggs, milk, and dairy products**. These are complete proteins that contain all essential amino acids.
 
• Plant-based protein sources include **soy products (tofu, edamame), lentils, chickpeas, nuts, seeds, and whole grains**. These are crucial for vegetarians and vegans.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Protein-Rich Foods:**
 
 
• **Eggs:** A single large egg contains approximately **6 grams of protein**. Eggs are also rich in healthy fats, vitamins, and minerals.
 
• **Chicken:** A 100-gram serving of chicken breast provides about **31 grams of protein**. It is low in fat and high in essential nutrients.
 
• **Almonds:** A 28-gram serving of almonds provides around **6 grams of protein**, along with healthy fats and fiber.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Daily Protein Requirement:**

 
 
• The **Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA)** for protein is approximately **0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight** for the average adult.
 
• Athletes or individuals engaging in heavy physical activity may require **1.2 to 2.0 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight**.
 
 
 
• **Potential Risks of Low Protein Intake:**
 
 
• Low protein intake can lead to **muscle loss, weakened immune function, and delayed wound healing**.
 
• Severe protein deficiency may cause a condition known as **kwashiorkor**, characterized by edema, fatigue, and stunted growth in children.

questions.question: Cereals such as wheat, rice, maize, millets and sorghum mainly provide us
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Cereals such as wheat, rice, maize, millets, and sorghum are primary sources of **carbohydrates** in our diet.
 
• Carbohydrates provide the main source of energy for the body, especially for the brain and muscles during physical activity.
 
• These cereals are rich in starch, which is a complex carbohydrate that breaks down into glucose in the body.
 
• Besides energy, carbohydrates play a crucial role in the **metabolic processes** of the body.
 
• Whole grains of these cereals also provide dietary fiber, which aids in digestion and helps prevent constipation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Proteins**

 
 
• Although cereals provide some protein, they are not a complete source of protein and often need to be paired with legumes to meet dietary requirements.
 
 
 
• **Fats**
 
 
• Cereals contain very small amounts of fats, primarily in the form of essential fatty acids found in the germ of the grain.
 
 
 
• **Vitamins and Minerals**
 
 
• Cereals are a good source of B vitamins, such as thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which are essential for energy metabolism.
 
• They also provide important minerals like iron, magnesium, and selenium, but the bioavailability of these nutrients can be affected by the presence of phytic acid in whole grains.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are a prerequisite for an efficient dairy farm management?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Animal husbandry** is the agricultural practice of breeding and raising livestock.
 
• India and China together have more than 70% of the world livestock population.
 
• However, India contributes only 25% to the world farm produce.
 
• This is because the productivity per unit is very low.
 
• In order **to improve our food production**, more **scientific and professional approaches** are being implemented nowadays.

• **Farm management** is an important aspect of improving food production.
 
• Dairy farm management involves management of animals for milk and its products for human consumption.
 
• There are certain **prerequisites for maintaining high yield and quality**:

 
• **Selection of good breeds** - 

 
 
• Milk yield primarily depends on the quality of the breed.
 
• We need to select a breed that is **high-yielding** under the prevailing conditions of the particular area.
 
• The breed should also be **resistant to diseases**.
 
 
 
• **Caring for cattle** - 
 
 
• The cattle should be housed well with adequate water.
 
• It should be maintained in disease-free conditions.
 
• **Scientific feeding** - refers to appropriate feeding with regard to both quantity and quality.
 
 
 
• **Maintenance of standards** - 
 
 
• A healthy farm results from regular maintenance.
 
• Hence, it should be kept **clean and hygienic** throughout the processes of milking, transport and storage.
 
• There should be **regular visits from a veterinary doctor** to check for cattle health.
 
• There should be **regular inspection** to check if the farm is being managed properly.
 
 

Therefore, **all the given options are ****prerequisite for an efficient dairy farm management**.

questions.question:
Which of the following problems arise if excessive fertilisers are used?

1. Water pollution

2. Destruction of soil fertility

Choose the correct code.
questions.solution:
**__Concept:__**

Fertilizers are absorbed by plants through the soil and can enter the food chain. As a result, fertiliser pollutes the water, soil, and air.

__**Explanation**:__ Too much fertilizer can be harmful. They lead to-

 
• Reduce the organic matter in the soil, leading to soil acidification.
 
• Deplete the **soil of key minerals(decrease soil fertility)**, resulting in lower vitamin and mineral content in food crops.
 
• Release the greenhouse gas nitrous oxide into the air.
 
• As a result of heavy nitrogen fertiliser use, the **amount of nitrate in drinking water(water pollution)** and rivers may rise.
 
• Increased availability of nutrients, notably N and P, increases the number of plants and algae in a lake, pond, or other water body.
 
• Manure has enough nitrogen and phosphorus to be utilised as a fertiliser for agricultural growth, and it will have a similar impact on algae and aquatic plants.

So, both **water pollution** and **destruction of soil fertility** problems arise if excessive fertilisers are used.

questions.question: Iron, iodine and zinc can be considered as which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micronutrients**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Macronutrients**__ in animal nutrition include carbohydrates, proteins, and fats, which are required in large amounts for energy, growth, and maintenance of body functions.

 __
 
• Minerals such as calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium are also considered** macrominerals. **
 
• Since iron, iodine, and zinc are required in much smaller amounts than these macronutrients, they do not fall into this category.
 
 
 
• Micronutrient__
 __
 
• Micronutrients are nutrients required in much smaller amounts compared to macronutrients.​
 
• **Iron (Fe):** Iron is a critical component of hemoglobin, which is responsible for oxygen transport in the blood. It is also part of various enzymes and proteins involved in energy production and metabolism. A deficiency of iron can lead to anemia and other health issues.
 
• **Iodine (I): **Iodine is essential for the production of thyroid hormones, which regulate metabolism, growth, and development. A deficiency in iodine can lead to goiter and hypothyroidism, affecting the overall health and metabolic rate of the animal.
 
• **Zinc (Zn)**: Zinc is involved in numerous aspects of cellular metabolism, acts as a cofactor for over 300 enzymes, and plays a role in immune function, protein synthesis, wound healing, DNA synthesis, and cell division. Zinc deficiency can impair growth, immune function, and reproduction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Steroid hormone inducers **are substances that influence the production or action of steroid hormones (like cortisol, estrogen, testosterone). This category does not apply to iron, iodine, or zinc as these minerals do not directly induce steroid hormone production.

questions.question: Which among the following is the source of protein?
questions.solution:
We living beings need different kinds of nutrients for our survival and the different mechanisms of the body. There is a range of nutrients that are obtained from different sources. Carbohydrates, **proteins**, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water are the nutrients present in the food. But these nutrients are not present in the same amount in various foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Protein is the chief component of all body tissues. We obtain proteins mainly from animal foods like milk and milk products, meat, fish, and egg.** Pulses and nuts are also good sources of protein. **

__
 
• Pulses are a rich source of proteins.
 
• Protein is one such nutrient required for the growth of our body.
 
• It can be obtained from plants as well as animal sources.

**Hence, Pulse is the source of protein. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] Hint__** 

__
 
• Wheat and Rice are rich sources of carbohydrates.
 
• Orange is a rich source of Vitamin C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** There are three important functions of proteins.

 
• **For growth and maintenance:** Proteins are required for the growth and maintenance of the body tissues. More protein is required by the body during periods of growth if needed to build up new tissues. 
 
• **Regulation of body processes: **Many body processes are controlled by the presence of proteins in the body. For this, proteins present in the form of enzymes and hormones help to regulate a number of important body processes. 
 
• **Proteins as a source of energy: **One gram of protein provides four Kcal. But protein foods are expensive sources of energy. As already explained under carbohydrates, it is preferable to use proteins for bodybuilding only, by providing enough carbohydrates and fats in the diet so that proteins are spared

questions.question: The macro-nutrient provided by inorganic fertilization are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen, Phosphorous, Potassium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nitrogen (N)**: Promotes leaf growth and forms proteins and chlorophyll.
 
• **Phosphorous (P)**: Aids in the development of roots, flowers, seeds, and fruit.
 
• **Potassium (K)**: Enhances overall plant health, improves drought resistance, and boosts disease resistance.
 
• These three nutrients are commonly referred to as **macronutrients** and are crucial for plant growth and development.
 
• Inorganic fertilizers typically contain these nutrients in various formulations to enhance soil fertility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Macronutrients vs. Micronutrients:**

 
 
• Macronutrients are required in larger quantities compared to micronutrients, which are needed in trace amounts.
 
• Micronutrients include elements such as iron, manganese, zinc, copper, molybdenum, and boron.
 
 
 
• **Role of Nitrogen:**
 
 
• Essential for the synthesis of amino acids and proteins.
 
• Vital for photosynthesis as it is a component of chlorophyll.
 
 
 
• **Role of Phosphorous:**
 
 
• Crucial for energy transfer in plants through ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
• Important for root development and flowering.
 
 
 
• **Role of Potassium:**
 
 
• Regulates water uptake and loss in plants.
 
• Activates enzymes involved in photosynthesis and respiration.
 
 
 
• **Inorganic Fertilizers:**
 
 
• Common types include ammonium nitrate, superphosphate, and potassium chloride.
 
• They are synthesized through chemical processes and provide readily available nutrients to plants.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about adding organic manures to the soil

A. They make the soil rigid so as to hold the plants firmly.

B. They add inorganic matter to the soil which is considered very rich in plant nutrient.

C. They improve the texture of the soil.

D. They enhance the water holding capacity of the soil.

The correct statements are:
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Manure** is an organic substance obtained from the decomposition of plant or animal wastes.
 
• The process of adding manure to the fields to replenish the soil with nutrients. This process is called **manuring.**

The advantages of adding manure into the fields are:

 
• **It enhances the water holding capacity of the soil.**
 
• it makes the soil porous due to which exchange of gases becomes easy.
 
• it increases the number of friendly microbes.
 
• **it improves the texture of the soil.**
 
• **It adds inorganic matter to the soil which is considered very rich in plant nutrient.**

Thereby,** the correct statements are B, C & D.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] Confusion Points__**They add inorganic matter to the soil which is considered very rich in plant nutrients:

__
 
• When organic matter like dead leaves or small insects is added to the soil they will degrade and beak into simple elements or compounds of** Na, N, C, etc.** 
 
• Also, note that all carbon compounds are not organic. 
 
• So, the given answer is correct. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Differences between Fertiliser and Manure

 
 

 **Fertiliser **
 **Manure**
 
 

 A fertiliser is an inorganic salt.
 Manure is a natural substance obtained by the decomposition of cattle dung, human waste and plant residues.
 
 

 A fertiliser is prepared in factories.
 Manure can be prepared in the field.
 
 

 A fertiliser does not provide any humus to the soil.
 Manure provides a lot of humus to the soil.
 
 

 Fertilisers are very rich in plant nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus & potassium.
 Manure is relatively less rich in plant nutrients
